title: The strategist — where the edge lives
card: The first seat page: five edges priced in 36ths — pips, corners, harbours, the robber, the deck — closing on the opening algorithm as a console.
lede: Five edges, every one a base-game number: the 2d6 triangle, the 14-pip corner, the 2:1 harbour, the robber's 5/36, and a deck that is 56% knights. The page closes on the opening algorithm — the three machines a strategist runs before placing a single road.
handle: An edge is a number the table didn't compute — and Catan prints most of them on the tokens: five dots on the 6 and the 8. The strategist is the player who reads the board in 36ths.
source: Catan base-game rules and their arithmetic (3–4 player set): 36 dice outcomes, 54 intersections, 9 harbours (4 generic 3:1 + 5 special 2:1), 25 development cards (14 knights · 5 VP · 2+2+2 utility).
